title: Egg White Omelet, Scrambled or Fried with Butter

content.title: About
content.content: Egg white omelet, scrambled or fried with butter is a dish made from pure egg whites cooked in butter. Egg whites provide high‑quality protein with virtually no fat or carbs, while butter adds a rich flavor and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg whites contain almost all essential amino acids.
Cooking in butter enhances absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin D.
Egg white protein is highly digestible, making it popular among athletes.
Butter gives a distinctive taste that is hard to replicate with other fats.
Egg white omelets are often used in diet plans because of their low calorie density.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Egg whites provide about 10 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat and carbohydrates
items.content: 100 g of egg whites contain virtually no fat or carbs, suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Contains vitamin B2 (riboflavin)
items.content: Riboflavin is involved in energy metabolism and supports healthy skin and eyes.

items.title: Supports immune function
items.content: Proteins and selenium in egg whites help maintain a normal immune response.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Egg white protein is quickly absorbed, making it ideal post‑workout.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg whites, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High cholesterol in butter
items.content: Butter contains saturated fat and cholesterol; excessive use may raise LDL levels.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Using non‑fresh eggs can lead to salmonella contamination.

items.title: Low vitamin D content
items.content: Egg whites contain little vitamin D, so additional sources are needed for adequate intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Whisk egg whites, add a pinch of salt and optional herbs. Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat, pour the mixture, and cook to the desired consistency—from soft scrambled to firm omelet. Serve with vegetables, herbs, or a sprinkle of low‑fat cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked omelet in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Raw egg whites should be kept refrigerated in their original packaging and used within 3–5 days.
